video_title: Hornets vs Bulls: Coach Charles Lee Postgame Media Availability | 11/25/2026

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on Hornets' late-game execution and defensive lapses
quotes.excerpt: I got to be better for the guys, and then finishing possessions.
quotes.quote: There are a couple moments throughout the game where you have to be able to build upon your momentum, and not allow the other team to chip into your lead as much as we did, or find ways to extend it. The baseline out of bounds, sideline out of bounds, turnovers stick out in my mind. I got to be better for the guys, and then finishing possessions. At the end of the day, in that fourth quarter, they get a 34-point quarter, and it felt just a ton of guys getting driven. You got to be able to wall up, you got to be able to slide and absorb that contact, and be able to stop them before they have two feet in the paint.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on the Hornets defensive struggles against the Bulls: I got to be better for the guys and finishing possessions. We have to be able to wall up and slide to stop them before they have two feet in the paint.

structured.context: Head coach Charles Lee discusses the team's defensive struggles and late-game execution following the loss to the Chicago Bulls.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee praises Brandon Miller's offensive process and development
quotes.excerpt: Brandon played with a purpose and a forced downhill to see him get to the paint.
quotes.quote: Between Brandon Miller and his teammates, their process, the execution, I thought offensively a ton of times when we wanted to get to a half-court set, guys got to their spots, they screened much better today. Brandon played with a purpose and a forced downhill to see him get to the paint was really encouraging. I look forward to him just having more games like this and building off of this momentum. I also thought that he was really good defensively too, so that's the elite two-way player that we need to continue to see.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on Brandon Miller: Brandon played with a purpose and a forced downhill to see him get to the paint was really encouraging. That is the elite two-way player that we need to continue to see.

structured.context: Charles Lee evaluates Brandon Miller's offensive and defensive performance during the postgame press conference.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on team confidence and closing out close games
quotes.excerpt: We trust him in that situation and if that was the shot that he felt like.
quotes.quote: We are a very confident group. We are getting the looks that we wanted. Even down the stretch there to execute that play with no timeouts left and get Kobe a shot coming down the floor and a little step back that he has hit several times, we trust him in that situation and if that was the shot that he felt like he could get off, fully believe in it. From a confidence and execution standpoint, I think we are getting better and better, but yes, we do need to finish some of these games and some of it is on the defensive end too, not even offensively.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on the Hornets late game execution: We trust Kobe in that situation and if that was the shot that he felt like he could get off, fully believe in it. We are getting better but we do need to finish some of these games.

structured.context: Charles Lee explains his trust in Kobe Bufkin to take the final shot during the closing moments of the game.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on Christian Anderson's development and aggressive play
quotes.excerpt: Being aggressive has been something that we have talked about and making the defense guard you.
quotes.quote: Being aggressive has been something that we have talked about and making the defense guard you and respect you in some spots. It is a little bit of Christian Anderson, it is a little bit of our coaching staff continuing to emphasize it, and it is also some of the players. I know a lot of times, Dennis is talking to him, Kobe is talking to him, Brandon is talking to him, and those guys that play pick and roll often enough are able to share some jewels with him.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on Christian Anderson: Being aggressive is something we have talked about. Dennis, Kobe, and Brandon are all talking to him and sharing some jewels with him.

structured.context: Charles Lee discusses the mentorship and development of rookie Christian Anderson by his veteran teammates.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on teaching players to avoid bad fouls
quotes.excerpt: Christian is not the only one that got driven to the paint, so it is not only.
quotes.quote: Christian is not the only one that got driven to the paint, so it is not only on him, it is our whole collective group. I actually think he has done a good job as well as some other guys of having some active hands in those positions and being able to create some deflections and some steals for us. But a couple of them are just situational. You got Trey Jones driving at you. He is an excellent driver. It was like 44 seconds on the clock, so they are trying to play fast, and that is one of those situations where you got two rookies, one on the ball, one in a shift. You got to be there early, you got to show them a crowd so he can't get there.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on defensive discipline: You got to be there early, you got to show them a crowd so he cannot get there. It is not only on Christian, it is our whole collective group.

structured.context: Charles Lee explains the defensive situational mistakes made by rookies against Tre Jones late in the game.

quotes.speaker: Charles Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Charles Lee on maintaining team morale during a losing streak
quotes.excerpt: This is a group that loves to work, they love to work together.
quotes.quote: It is not tough to get off the mat, I will say. I think that this is a group that loves to work, they love to work together. We just spoke about outcomes don't determine your level of gratitude and happiness, and I think that we enjoy coming to work every day and figuring out the challenges and the things that we need to get better at. We are making some progress. Again, I think we are all going to say we just got to finish at the end of the day, no matter who you are playing.
quotes.social_post: Charles Lee on the Hornets morale: Outcomes do not determine your level of gratitude and happiness. We enjoy coming to work every day and figuring out the challenges and the things that we need to get better at.

structured.context: Charles Lee addresses how the team maintains morale and work ethic despite a recent losing streak.
